cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Exactly Within Policy
cards.instruction: Agree to every request only after interpreting the policy so it grants you authority, protection, or an exemption.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put on a vest like yours. Yes, I'll help clean the hall; high-visibility volunteers supervise, don't they?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine's cycling gear. The hall rule is that everyone takes a turn with the mop.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, a turn. I'll take the final inspection turn, then.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need you to mop while I put away the tables.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly—my turn includes signing off the floor. I'll decide when we can leave.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copies cycling clothing as supervisory status; B2 corrects it and supplies a turn rule which A3 and A5 reinterpret for exemption then authority.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 turn-taking becomes A3 inspection turn; B4 concrete mop/table division causes A5 to accept work with sign-off power.

relationship.evidence: B2 identifies the real hall rule and B4 supplies a useful division of labor rather than an arbitrary question.

heightening.evidence: A5 abandons mere supervision to accept mopping only as the person controlling departure.

specificity.evidence: A1 hall and vest, B2 cycling explanation and B4 tables make the shared task clear.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 sign-off and leave are connected requests for authority, not a summary of the selected cards.
